items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: I think Tommy Bell was enamored with Burt Bacharach.

ctx.x: You know I think the big difference between Motown and Philly Sound was Motown was the sound of the young America. It was really a youth movement. R&B. Whereas the Philly sound was a sophisticated, much jazzier much more adult kind of a sound. I mean I've always thought that MFSB could have been the Lionel Hampton band. You know? And in turn, in a way, I was right. MFSB could have gone and played behind Frank Sinatra or anybody. You know? I mean it was that adept at a lot of different styles and adult styles. And…

mean I think Tommy Bell was enamored with Burt Bacharach. And Burt Bacharach was very sophisticated you know? And I think a lot of Thom's arrangements back in those days were like Bacharach arrangements. They would feature a horn player or feature a flute or feature — I mean feature a harp. I mean he had his way of introducing symphonic instruments. And in the '70s, early '70s, that was a big deal I think.
Who was he writing for previous to this? Do you know?
